task.description:
WF-03 Step 2 (fix design) for ISS-0119. Write the design artefact to `lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md`. Design only -- no implementation, no finished replacement prose pasted in as if it were the artefact's own content is fine ONLY where the design is specifying exact required wording (see 'What a design means here' below).

READ THE STEP 1 DIAGNOSIS FIRST (`step-01-issue-fixer-diagnose.json`, result.summary). It is long and it is load-bearing. Do not re-derive its measurements; do re-check anything you intend to rely on structurally. Its established facts, which you may take as given:
  - The file is 361,376 bytes / 5,766 lines / 182 entries. A whole-file Read is REFUSED outright (error quoted verbatim in the handoff), not truncated. It first crossed the limit at commit 3d19e8c on 2026-08-18T15:32:52Z, so the safeguard has been unexecutable for ~2.5 days.
  - MACHINE-PARSED CONSUMERS: ZERO. mix.exs:50 and scripts/timed_test.sh:8 are comments; .github/ has no reference. A split breaks no code and no gate. This is real design freedom.
  - 23 LIVE INSTRUCTION SITES across 12 files tell an agent to read or append to this file (doc-updater.md carries 4, core-directives.md 3, WF-02 3, AGENT_SYSTEM.md 3). The full enumeration is in the Step 1 handoff -- use it.
  - ~103 immutable historical references under handoffs/ and test/reports/ that cannot be retro-edited, plus ONE line-number citation that a split would silently falsify: lib/letflow/design/iss-0078-pin-rebind-provenance.md:367 cites `docs/status/requirement_status.yaml:5158`.
  - SCHEMA HAS ALREADY DRIFTED, and pre-dates the size problem: `SCOPE-CHANGE` appears 31x as a `req:` value and 3x as an `event:` value (lines 3490/3577/3744, all ORCH, 2026-08-17). The header documents 3 `event` values; 7 are in use (done 107, started 54, cancelled 8, blocked 5, revised 4, SCOPE-CHANGE 3, verified 1). `req: ISS-NNNN` has zero precedent.
  - docs/agents/protocols/TASK_QUEUE.md:133 instructs recording a reconciliation 'as a SCOPE-CHANGE event' -- the WRONG FIELD versus 31 entries of `req:` practice. The 3 divergent entries are the ones that followed the written rule. This is a documented instruction actively producing the drift.

SCOPE DECISION MADE BY ORCH, do not relitigate: ISSUE-FIXER reported two MINOR incidental findings. Finding (1) -- the `event` vocabulary drift and the TASK_QUEUE.md:133 wrong-field instruction -- IS IN SCOPE for this run. It is the same header-documentation defect as ISS-0119's own second gap, in the same header, and shipping a rewritten header that still under-documents the vocabulary would leave the file wrong in the same way. Finding (2) -- ISS-0119's own stale line/precedent counts -- is bookkeeping for DOC-UPDATER at Step 6, not a design input.

YOUR DECISION TO MAKE. ISS-0119 proposes two remedies and explicitly declines to prescribe: (a) make the file readable again -- split by period with an index, or otherwise bound its growth, preserving the full history since this is audit trail and nothing may be dropped; (b) rewrite the header so it prescribes an EXECUTABLE safeguard rather than one assuming a full read -- naming the exact scoped-read technique that reveals the schema, and stating the conventions explicitly. Choose (a), (b), or both, and JUSTIFY the choice against the diagnosis. Two constraints on that choice: ISS-0119 explicitly forbids resolving this by relaxing the append-only rule (the rule is correct; the mechanism supporting it degraded), and whatever you choose MUST close the core-directives.md:173 vs :328 precedence gap -- as it stands an agent has two rules pointing opposite ways for this one file and nothing saying which wins.

WHAT A DESIGN MEANS HERE. This is a docs/process change, not Elixir, so the usual 'interfaces and @specs' shape does not apply literally. Your artefact must instead specify, precisely enough that ELIXIR-DEV/DOC-UPDATER can execute it without inventing anything:
  - Every file to be changed or created, by path, and for each: exactly what changes.
  - If you choose a split: the exact split boundary rule, the index file's structure, what happens to the original path, and how a reader resolves an old citation (including the :5158 line reference and the ~103 historical mentions). State explicitly how the split is performed such that NO entry is dropped, and how that is verified afterwards.
  - The exact required NEW header text for whatever file(s) an agent appends to. Quote it in full -- this is the one place finished prose belongs in this artefact, because the whole defect is that the current header prescribes an unexecutable procedure. The new procedure must be one an agent can actually run today and must be stated as concrete commands or tool calls, not as an aspiration.
  - The full documented vocabulary: every legal `req:` value including SCOPE-CHANGE, every legal `event:` value with the 7 actually in use accounted for, and what to do about the 3 malformed entries. NOTE CONSTRAINT C2 from the diagnosis: nothing may be dropped and the 3 malformed entries must NOT be silently normalized, since that would itself be the rewrite this whole safeguard exists to prevent. Design how they are handled honestly.
  - Which of the 23 instruction sites must be edited and what each must say afterwards, including the TASK_QUEUE.md:133 field correction.
  - How the fix behaves at the NEXT growth threshold (diagnosis constraint C7) -- a fix that merely resets the clock is a worse outcome than one that defines what happens when the limit is next approached.
  - What the Step 4 regression test can actually assert. This is docs, so there is no ExUnit assertion of prose -- but a mechanically checkable invariant may well exist (for example: that no appendable status file exceeds the read limit, or that every entry's `req`/`event` value is in the documented vocabulary). Propose what is checkable and where it would live; if you conclude nothing mechanical is checkable, say so explicitly and justify it, because that materially changes what Step 4 can do.

Do not write the implementation. Do not edit docs/status/requirement_status.yaml, core-directives.md, or any of the 23 sites in this step -- the artefact describes the change; ELIXIR-DEV performs it at Step 3.

=== REWORK ITERATION 1 (dispatched by ORCH 2026-08-21T05:16Z, after CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR returned FAIL at Step 2b) ===

The freeze-and-roll shape is CORRECT and was independently verified by the gate -- do NOT redesign it. The gate opened iss-0078-pin-rebind-provenance.md:367 itself, confirmed it cites requirement_status.yaml:5158, confirmed sed -n '5158p' lands inside the REQ-059/PIN-05 note body, confirmed EOF is line 5,766, and confirmed an EOF-only append shifts nothing above it. C4 holds by construction. It also confirmed via git show --stat 24e7087 that no target file was touched. Checks 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 11 all PASSED. These are local edits to lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md, not a new design.

BLOCKER (Step 2 AC7 -- 'the procedure it prescribes is executable today as concrete commands or tool calls'). Section 4 opens with 'Every command below is runnable today on this repo.' That is false on this host's primary shell, and the gate verified it empirically rather than inferring it: `grep --version` in PowerShell returns 'The term grep is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet, function, script file, or operable program' (CommandNotFoundException). Section 4's HOW-TO-APPEND step 1 is a bare GNU-grep invocation given WITHOUT a shell label -- `grep -n 'status: current' -B 2 docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml` -- while steps 2, 3 and the roll-rule block are correctly given as Bash/PowerShell pairs, so this is an omission rather than a misunderstanding. A DOC-UPDATER turn on PowerShell therefore fails on the FIRST step of the very procedure whose purpose is executability, and has to improvise unaided -- the exact failure shape the Step 1 diagnosis documented and the exact defect ISS-0119 exists to remove. FIX: give step 1 a labelled shell pair (suggested PowerShell form: `Select-String -Path docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml -Pattern 'status: current' -Context 2,0`), following the both-shells precedent core-directives.md:156-161 already sets, and sweep Sections 10.2 and 10.3's 'targeted grep/sed' and 'grep/sed/awk only' replacement prose for the same single-shell assumption.

MAJOR (WF-03 Step 4's fail-first requirement). Section 7 gives TEST-DESIGNER no way to demonstrate the property WF-03 Step 4 demands: 'the test must be shown to fail against the pre-fix code and pass against the post-fix code... checked out the pre-fix commit, ran the new test, confirms it failed.' Section 7 states every assertion is derived from the index file so the test never hardcodes a volume list -- but docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml does not exist at 3d19e8c or at any pre-fix commit, so running the new test on the pre-fix tree errors on a MISSING INDEX rather than failing A3's size check. That is a failure any test of any new file would produce, and it proves nothing about coverage of this bug. The claim that A3 'would have failed on 2026-08-18 at 3d19e8c' is arithmetically sound (4,217 lines / 264,861 bytes, over both ceilings) but it is a counterfactual, not a runnable demonstration. FIX: specify in Section 7 a concrete fail-first procedure -- which artefact stands in for the pre-fix state (a fixture index under test/fixtures/, an A3 size-check helper callable against an arbitrary path, or `git show 3d19e8c:docs/status/requirement_status.yaml` into a temp file), where it lives, and how A3 is exercised against it. This is a design decision that changes the test's shape, so TEST-DESIGNER must not have to invent it.

MINOR 1. Section 8 step 5 and Section 3.3 specify frozen_prefix_sha256 as SHA-256 over lines 1-5766 with CRLF normalised to LF -- unambiguous on line endings (the gate explicitly did NOT flag this as MAJOR) but silent on whether a trailing line terminator follows line 5,766 in the hashed byte stream. Join-with-LF and terminate-with-LF give different digests, and the digest's purpose is reproducibility by a later agent. Write the convention down.

MINOR 2. Restatement hazard: the ceilings (1,200 lines / 120,000 bytes) appear in FIVE places -- the index roll_rule, every volume header, the core-directives.md:328 replacement (10.3), the doc-updater.md:31 replacement (10.2) and the anti-patterns.md replacement (10.5) -- while A3 reads them only from the index and A8 checks only vocabulary. A later ceiling change leaves up to four prose copies stale with nothing to detect it. Either extend A8 to assert the current volume's header quotes the same ceilings as roll_rule, or replace the prose numbers with a pointer to the index.

MINOR 3. Two counting slips. (a) Section 11's 'Modified (10)' enumerates 9 distinct files -- the list is exhaustive, only the count is wrong, but ELIXIR-DEV's own file-count check at Step 3 would then disagree with the design. (b) Section 4 step 2 states both bounds but its Bash form reports lines only while its PowerShell form reports bytes only; the roll-rule block already gives both measurements in both shells and step 2 should match it.

FOR THE RECORD, not a defect in your artefact: this handoff's original task text said Section 10 claims '14 EDIT with post-edit text and 9 NO CHANGE'. The gate counted the table mechanically and found 15 EDIT + 8 NO CHANGE across the 23 numbered sites (16 EDIT across 24 rows, the extra row being the core-directives.md:173 back-reference your design correctly ADDS on top of the diagnosis's list). All 23 diagnosis sites are present and correctly dispositioned. The 14/9 figure came from your own result.summary and ORCH propagated it into the gate's brief; correct it in your summary on this pass so it stops travelling.

CHANGE-APPROACH NOTE (ORCHESTRATOR.md section 5): this is iteration 1 of 3 and the gate's findings are specific and local, so repeating the same design with these five edits applied IS the correct approach here. If a second FAIL returns on the same executability ground, do not patch a third time -- change strategy, e.g. stop hand-writing per-shell command pairs and specify a single committed script both shells invoke.

When you complete this rework, append your rework account to result.summary in the established form -- ' || REWORK ITERATION 1 (<timestamp>), addressing CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR FAIL. ...' -- rather than rewriting the original summary, matching the convention in handoffs/WF01-S3-EXPANSION-20260818/step-01-req-analyst.json.

=== REWORK ITERATION 2 (dispatched by ORCH 2026-08-21T05:33Z, after CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR re-gate pass 2 returned FAIL) ===

ITERATION 1 WAS LARGELY SUCCESSFUL AND THIS IS NOT THE STRATEGY-CHANGE CONDITION. R1, the executability BLOCKER, is FIXED and the gate confirmed it by execution rather than by reading: it ran your PowerShell form on this host and got ObjectNotFound/ItemNotFoundException attributed to SelectStringCommand -- the cmdlet resolved, -Path/-Pattern/-Context 2,0 parsed, and only the file layer failed, which is the correct outcome given the index does not exist yet. It then swept all 905 lines itself (22 hits on grep|sed|awk|wc|head|tail|date|cat|sha256sum, each inspected in context) and found ZERO surviving single-shell commands and no remaining line-continuations. It singled out the Section 4 preamble's forward-binding rule as the thing that makes the fix durable rather than a patch. You also swept further than you were asked to. R3, R4 and R5 are all fixed and independently re-verified -- the gate RAN two of the three digest reference forms and got matching output (5a1a64ab0b999da3fd86be90109ecee46b9d538d9e9945c0d39fddb10075a804, recorded so Step 3 has an independent cross-check), and grepped all 905 lines for the ceilings confirming zero unchecked prose copies survive. Your Section 10.1 count correction is present and matches the gate's own mechanical recount exactly. R2's second-order checks all passed: the six signatures are complete, no function hardcodes the index location, and the gate OPENED mix.exs and confirmed line 20 really is `defp elixirc_paths(:test), do: ["lib", "test/support"]`, so no build-config change is needed.

ONE BLOCKER REMAINS, and it is the ruling in Section 7.1, not the section's analysis.

BLOCKER (WF-03 Step 4 fail-first, unresolved). A3b does not demonstrate the property. Two independent reasons, either fatal on its own:

(1) IT IS NOT DIRECTIONAL. docs/status/requirement_status.yaml was over BOTH ceilings before the fix (4,217 lines / 264,861 bytes at 3d19e8c) and is over BOTH ceilings after it (5,766 / 361,376). within_bounds?/3 therefore returns {:error, %{over: [:lines, :bytes]}} in the pre-fix world AND in the post-fix world, so the assertion is GREEN IN BOTH. A test that passes identically with and without the fix cannot be the fail-first proof of anything -- it never fails, so there is no 'fails against pre-fix code' half at all.

(2) IT IS THE TAUTOLOGY. Under the fix that file is frozen, is no longer the append target, is pinned by A6, and is EXPECTED to be oversized by design. Section 7.1's own sentence -- 'Volume 1 is frozen and covered by A6, so these numbers cannot drift' -- is the proof that its subject cannot change. Asserting a frozen artefact still has the size it is frozen at restates the freeze; it does not test a regression.

WF-03 Step 4's words, which the design must satisfy rather than reinterpret: 'Step 4's test must be shown to fail against the pre-fix code and pass against the post-fix code -- TEST-DESIGNER states this explicitly in the test spec (checked out the pre-fix commit, ran the new test, confirms it failed; then confirms it passes on the fix branch).' The optional git-show block in 7.1 does not rescue this, and the gate's reason is sharper than 'optional may not run': Section 7.1 makes an affirmative RULING that a mandatory workflow obligation needs no performance. TEST-DESIGNER has no authority to override that ruling, so leaving it stands as a design instruction to skip a gate -- which core-directives.md's Instruction Precedence forbids at every level ('A safety/gate rule is never overridden by a more specific instruction').

KEEP WHAT IS RIGHT. Section 7.1's diagnosis of why a naive pre-fix checkout proves nothing IS correct, and its 'Rejected alternatives' paragraph (the oversized synthetic fixture; git show as the primary mechanism failing on a shallow clone) is correct and worth keeping so neither is re-proposed. A3b itself is worth KEEPING TOO -- but relabelled honestly. It is a detector-calibration guard: it would fail if the helper's measurement regressed or if someone raised the ceilings past the frozen volume's real size. That is genuine value; it is simply not the fail-first proof, and Section 7.1 must stop describing it as sufficient on its own.

THE DESIGN DECISION IS YOURS, and it is a real one -- pick ONE and write it into Section 7.1. The gate named two viable routes; you may propose a third if it satisfies Step 4's language better. (A) Promote the `git show 3d19e8c:docs/status/requirement_status.yaml` extraction from optional to MANDATORY and make it part of the Step 4 record, specifying where the extracted artefact lives, how the helper is exercised against it, and what TEST-DESIGNER must quote. (B) Specify that current-volume resolution DEGRADES to docs/status/requirement_status.yaml when no index is present, so A3 itself -- the live assertion, unmodified -- fails pre-fix for exactly the right reason (the pre-fix current volume is over the ceiling) and passes post-fix (the current volume is v2, well under it). ORCH's read, offered as input and not as a decision: (B) is the more elegant of the two because it makes the fail-first property intrinsic to the assertion rather than bolted on beside it, and it removes the missing-index error the gate identified as the whole problem in pass 1 -- but (B) also introduces a fallback path that must not become a way for a future agent to append to volume 1, so if you choose it, state explicitly how that is prevented. Choose on the merits.

MINOR (cosmetic, introduced by iteration 1). Section 8's PowerShell digest form is an inline code span containing a literal backtick -- PowerShell's newline escape -- so markdown terminates the span early and the rendered command is truncated. The command itself is correct; the gate ran it. Fence it as a powershell code block instead. Fold this into the same pass.

SCOPE DISCIPLINE FOR THIS PASS: change Section 7.1's ruling and Section 8's fencing. Do not revisit R1, R3, R4, R5, the count correction, or the freeze-and-roll shape -- all are verified fixed and re-opening them risks regressing work the gate has already cleared twice. Append your account to result.summary as ' || REWORK ITERATION 2 (<timestamp>), addressing CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR re-gate pass 2 FAIL. ...' and set rework_count to 2.
acceptance_criteria: lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md exists and is the only file created or modified outside this handoff
The artefact states which remedy is chosen -- (a), (b), or both -- and justifies the choice against the Step 1 diagnosis rather than against ISS-0119's prose alone
The artefact closes the core-directives.md:173 vs :328 precedence gap explicitly, stating which rule wins for this file and where that ruling is written down
The artefact does NOT relax the append-only rule and says so
Every file to be changed or created is named by path with its exact required change

If a split is chosen: the split boundary rule, index structure, fate of the original path, old-citation resolution (including the :5158 line reference), the no-entry-dropped method and its verification are all specified
The exact required new header text is quoted in full, and the procedure it prescribes is executable today as concrete commands or tool calls
The full req: and event: vocabularies are documented, all 7 in-use event values accounted for, and the handling of the 3 malformed entries is designed without silently normalizing them
The TASK_QUEUE.md:133 wrong-field instruction is addressed
Behaviour at the next growth threshold is specified
A mechanically checkable invariant for Step 4 is proposed with its location, or its absence is explicitly justified
No implementation is performed -- no edits to docs/status/, core-directives.md, or any instruction site

result.summary:
WF-03 Step 2 fix design for ISS-0119 complete. Artefact: lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md (the only file created or modified by this step besides this handoff). No implementation performed: docs/status/requirement_status.yaml, core-directives.md and all 23 instruction sites are untouched.

=== REMEDY CHOSEN: BOTH (a) AND (b), AS ONE STEP 3 COMMIT ===

Justified against the Step 1 diagnosis, not ISS-0119's prose. (b) alone fails on the diagnosis's C7 ("it leaves C7 unaddressed -- the file keeps growing and the scoped-read window keeps covering a smaller fraction"): a header-only fix converts today's HARD failure (a refusal that announces itself) into a SOFT one (a compliant-looking partial read), which is strictly worse. (b) alone also cannot answer the diagnosis's strongest finding -- the three event: SCOPE-CHANGE entries were written 2026-08-17 at 234,147 bytes, while the full read still WORKED, proving "the read-in-full link was already weak as a schema-transmission mechanism before it broke outright." Prescribing a SCOPED read of a file whose schema a FULL read already failed to transmit cannot be the whole answer. (a) alone transmits no schema -- the diagnosis warns a split "multiplies the L2 problem" without the header carried into every shard -- and leaves the 23 sites, TASK_QUEUE.md:133 and the precedence gap untouched. One commit, because (a)'s site edits and (b)'s edits land in the same files; splitting across runs would leave instructions describing a layout that does not exist.

=== THE SHAPE: FREEZE-AND-ROLL, NOT A RETROACTIVE SPLIT ===

Driven by C4. Re-checked structurally for this design: line 5158 of the status file falls inside the note: prose of a REQ-059/PIN-05 entry, so ANY line inserted or removed above it silently falsifies iss-0078-pin-rebind-provenance.md:367. Therefore the existing file is NOT split, renamed, reordered, or edited above its last line. It is closed in place as VOLUME 1, byte-identical through line 5,766, with a closure footer APPENDED AT EOF (appending shifts nothing). New appends go to a new small VOLUME 2. C4 is satisfied by construction: all ~103 immutable historical references still resolve, and :5158 still points at the same characters -- no old-citation resolution scheme is needed because no citation is broken.

Layout: docs/status/requirement_status.yaml (v1, closed/frozen) + docs/status/requirement_status.v2.yaml (current) + docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml (NEW fixed-name entry point that every instruction site now points at, so no agent ever needs to know the volume-naming scheme).

NO-ENTRY-DROPPED METHOD: there is no data-moving step at all. All 182 entries stay in the file and at the line numbers they already occupy; the only write to v1 is comment lines at EOF. Verified at Step 3 by six quoted checks: git diff --numstat deletions must be 0; grep -c '^  - req: ' must still be 182; sed -n '5158p' must return the same text; sed -n '3490p;3577p;3744p' must still return three malformed lines; the frozen-prefix SHA-256 recorded in the index must verify; whole-commit numstat must show insertions-only for v1.

=== APPEND-ONLY RULE: NOT RELAXED, AND THE ARTEFACT SAYS SO EXPLICITLY (design section 1) ===

Strengthened rather than relaxed. Volume 1 becomes MORE protected: assertion A6 hashes its 5,766-line prefix, so a silent rewrite now fails the suite -- the first mechanical enforcement this rule has ever had (the diagnosis found "there is no second line of defence"). What changes is only which file the next append lands in and how large an APPENDABLE file may become -- the mechanism, not the rule.

=== PRECEDENCE GAP (core-directives.md:173 vs :328) CLOSED ===

RULING: :173's scoped-read rule is the general rule and governs every CLOSED volume and every other large file. The full-read requirement survives ONLY for the CURRENT volume, and only because the roll rule bounds that volume so the read stays executable. The design does not re-litigate the original resolution (the diagnosis showed it was deliberate and correct); it makes the winning branch AVAILABLE again and then states the fallback that was missing -- closed volumes are never appended to, so they never need a full read. Written down in THREE places so an agent hits it from any direction: core-directives.md:328 (primary, with a forward-reference to :173), core-directives.md:173 (back-reference to item 3, so an agent reading the general rule learns of the exception), and the index file's header. Both sites' exact replacement text is quoted in design section 10.3.

=== NEW HEADER TEXT: QUOTED IN FULL, EXECUTABLE TODAY (design section 4) ===

A six-step HOW TO APPEND procedure in concrete commands for both shells: (1) grep -n 'status: current' -B 2 on the index to confirm the target volume; (2) one un-scoped Read of the current volume, possible BY CONSTRUCTION, with an explicit STOP-and-file instruction if it is ever refused or truncated -- the fallback whose total absence was the diagnosis's core finding; (3) date -u / (Get-Date).ToUniversalTime() for the clock; (4) append; (5) git diff --numstat as a POSITIVE verification that the deletions count is 0; (6) the roll rule. Nothing is aspirational.

=== VOCABULARY FULLY DOCUMENTED; 3 MALFORMED ENTRIES HANDLED WITHOUT NORMALIZING ===

req: exactly two legal values -- REQ-NNN (151) and SCOPE-CHANGE (31). The header states outright that req: ISS-NNNN IS NOT LEGAL and has zero precedent across 182 entries, and that issue fixes use req: SCOPE-CHANGE with the ISS id in note: -- killing the obvious wrong guess ISS-0119 identified.
event: exactly six legal values, all 7 in-use values accounted for -- done 107, started 54, blocked 5, cancelled 8, revised 4, verified 1 documented as legal (cancelled/revised/verified were previously undocumented); SCOPE-CHANGE 3 declared NOT legal as an event.
The three malformed entries (v1 lines 3490/3577/3744) are NOT edited, now or ever; declared three times over (v1's closure footer, the index's known_anomalies:, the current volume's header); ATTRIBUTED to TASK_QUEUE.md:133 so a reader sees they were compliance with a wrong instruction; and MACHINE-PINNED by assertion A5, which asserts the on-disk anomaly set equals the declared set EXACTLY. That protects C2 in both directions: new drift fails, and a silent later normalization ALSO fails.

=== TASK_QUEUE.md:133 ADDRESSED ===

Exact replacement quoted (design 10.4): record as an entry with req: SCOPE-CHANGE and a normal event: value, plus an explicit "SCOPE-CHANGE is a req value, never an event value" and a note that the earlier wording produced the three malformed entries. TASK_QUEUE.md:379 also corrected to point at volume 1's req: SCOPE-CHANGE entries.

=== NEXT GROWTH THRESHOLD (C7) ===

Bound: current volume <= 1,200 lines AND <= 120,000 working-tree bytes -- ~60% of the Read tool's 2,000-line default and ~46% of its 262,144-byte limit. BOTH limits are respected, because a line-truncated read is the silent failure mode a byte-only bound would miss. Trigger: checked by DOC-UPDATER immediately AFTER its own append, so the volume that fills is closed by the agent that filled it, in the same commit -- no deferred cleanup and no chance for the next agent to hit a refusal. Second, independent trigger: assertion A3 fails mix test if any current volume is over bound, so the safeguard no longer rests solely on agent diligence. Unbounded: volume n names n+1, the index always names the current one, so there is no future threshold at which ISS-0119 recurs.

=== STEP 4 MECHANICAL INVARIANT: YES, ONE EXISTS ===

test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs -- ExUnit, no database, no new deps (stdlib line parsing plus :crypto). Eight assertions, all derived from the index so no volume list is hardcoded. A3 IS THE ISS-0119 REGRESSION ASSERTION: the current volume must be within the roll rule's bounds -- it would have FAILED on 2026-08-18 at commit 3d19e8c, 2.5 days before ISS-0119 was filed by hand. A6 (SHA-256 of each closed volume's frozen prefix, CRLF-normalized for platform stability) is the first mechanical enforcement of the append-only rule in this repo's history. Also A1 index/disk agreement, A2 exactly-one-current, A4 vocabulary conformance, A5 exact anomaly set, A7 volume-chain integrity, A8 header completeness.

=== SCOPE ===

ORCH's scope decision honoured: incidental finding (1) (event-vocabulary drift + TASK_QUEUE.md:133) is designed in full; finding (2) (ISS-0119's stale counts) is left to DOC-UPDATER at Step 6 and is not a design input. All 23 instruction sites are dispositioned in a table -- 14 EDIT with required post-edit text, 9 NO CHANGE with the reason each remains true (they survive precisely because v1's path and line numbers are unchanged). Step 3 touches 3 new files and 10 modified files, all named by path. Four open questions are recorded rather than silently resolved (volume naming, the ceiling values, whether the test also becomes a standalone mix letflow.check step, and the permanence of the anomalies); none blocks Step 3. || REWORK ITERATION 1 (2026-08-21T05:25:01Z), addressing CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR FAIL (1 BLOCKER, 1 MAJOR, 3 MINOR at step-02b). No redesign: the freeze-and-roll shape is unchanged, and the gate independently verified its central claim (iss-0078-pin-rebind-provenance.md:367 cites requirement_status.yaml:5158; EOF is line 5,766; an EOF-only append shifts nothing above it; git show --stat 24e7087 confirms no target file was touched). All five findings are local edits to lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md, now 905 lines (was 737). Still the only file created or modified by this step besides this handoff; docs/status/requirement_status.yaml, core-directives.md and all 23 instruction sites remain untouched.

BLOCKER (AC7, executability) FIXED, and fixed as a rule rather than as a one-line patch.
